article_title: FDA Approves Subcutaneous Starting Dose for Leqembi Iqlik, Bringing At-Home Initiation to Early Alzheimer's Treatment
summary: Automated checks all pass and every named/numeric claim traces cleanly to the six Eisai/Biogen/BioArctic/ADDF/StockTitan/BioSpace sources, but two subordinate issues require a public corrections note: (1) the Overview's 'roughly two months after the FDA had extended its review period' clause is cited to the Eisai/Biogen press release, which contains no mention of any review-period extension; (2) a bracketed direct quote attributed to BioSpace paraphrases rather than reproduces BioSpace's actual sentence on mild cognitive impairment.

findings.message: Unsourced regulatory-timeline claim in the Overview lead
findings.details: The second sentence of the Overview states the approval came 'roughly two months after the FDA had extended its review period,' citing the Eisai/Biogen PR Newswire release (source-0, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fda-approves-leqembi-iqlik-lecanemab-irmb-subcutaneous-injection-as-an-initiation-dose-for-early-alzheimers-disease-302824254.html) as the source. That release (and the identical copy at StockTitan/source-4, and the BioSpace copy/source-5) contains no reference to any review-period extension anywhere in its text. None of the other 5 cited sources mention it either. The core approval claim in the same sentence is well supported; only the 'extended review period' clause is unsupported by any cited source.

findings.message: Bracketed quote attributed to BioSpace paraphrases rather than reproduces the source verbatim
findings.details: Article text: '["the earliest symptomatic stage, characterized by subtle symptoms like forgetfulness and confusion."]' linked to the BioSpace snapshot (source-5). BioSpace's actual sentence reads: 'MCI due to AD is the earliest symptomatic stage of Alzheimer's disease and can appear with subtle symptoms such as forgetfulness, confusion, or feeling at a loss for words.' The quoted phrase does not appear verbatim anywhere in the BioSpace snapshot; it is a paraphrase presented inside quotation marks as a direct quote. The underlying fact (MCI is the earliest symptomatic stage, with symptoms like forgetfulness/confusion) is accurate and supported by every press-release source, so this is a quotation-fidelity issue, not a fabricated fact.

content_preview.title: FDA Approves Subcutaneous Starting Dose for Leqembi Iqlik, Bringing At-Home Initiation to Early Alzheimer's Treatment
content_preview.summary: The FDA cleared a subcutaneous starting dose for Eisai and Biogen's Leqembi Iqlik, letting early Alzheimer's patients begin anti-amyloid treatment with a 15-second at-home injection instead of IV infusion.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a subcutaneous starting dose for Leqembi Iqlik (lecanemab-irmb), letting patients with early Alzheimer's disease begin anti-amyloid treatment with an at-home autoinjector instead of an intravenous infusion, according to [Eisai and Biogen](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fda-approves-leqembi-iqlik-lecanemab-irmb-subcutaneous-injection-as-an-initiation-dose-for-early-alzheimers-disease-302824254.html). The companies announced...

recommendations: File a corrections record covering both issues so readers see the public trail: the unsupported 'FDA had extended its review period' timeline detail, and the paraphrased BioSpace quote on mild cognitive impairment.
For future submissions, when a bracketed passage is presented in quotation marks as a direct quote, verify it is character-for-character verbatim against the snapshot rather than a close paraphrase.

editor_notes.content_quality: 830-word News piece with clean Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Why It Matters structure. Dense, well-organized bulleted list of clinical and safety specifics with inline per-claim citations — a strong example of the house style. No sensationalism; appropriately caveats the unknowns (pricing, payer uptake).
editor_notes.source_verification: All 6 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200, sha256 of each decompressed snapshot verified against manifest.json). (1) source-0 PR Newswire / Eisai (302824254): confirms sBLA approval for once-weekly SC initiation dose, 500 mg as two 250 mg injections in ~15 seconds each, MCI/mild-dementia indication, 360 mg maintenance after 18 months IV/SC, 94% autoinjector ease-of-use, late-August 2026 launch via specialty pharmacy, Howard Fillit quote verbatim, full ARIA/ICH safety label. Does NOT contain any mention of an FDA review-period extension. (2) source-1 PR Newswire / BioArctic (302824479): confirms same approval facts from BioArctic's release; Gunilla Osswald quote verbatim ('This approval represents another important step forward in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.' / 'By providing a new administration option from the start of treatment, patients, caregivers and healthcare professionals gain greater flexibility in how therapy is delivered.'). (3) source-2 GlobeNewswire (AAIC clinical data, July 12, 2026): confirms 104% exposure ratio (90% CI 99.1%-109%) verbatim, the 'driven by lecanemab exposure rather than route of administration' quote verbatim, 1.4% anti-drug antibody incidence with no neutralizing antibodies, and patient-satisfaction ranges (75%-97% satisfaction, 83%-97% convenience, 92%-100% willingness to recommend) verbatim. (4) source-3 PR Newswire / ADDF: confirms Laura Nisenbaum quote verbatim, Isobel Coleman 'inflection point' quote verbatim, ~75% of pipeline on non-amyloid pathways ('nearly 75%' in source vs '75%' in article — immaterial rounding, not in quote marks), $400M/792 programs/21 countries figures, and the '~15 seconds vs hour-long IV infusions' framing verbatim. (5) source-4 StockTitan: full republication of the Eisai press release plus prescribing-information safety label; confirms all ARIA figures (21% vs 9% overall, ARIA-E 13% vs 2%, ARIA-H 17% vs 9%, symptomatic ARIA 3%, serious 0.7%) and the ApoE ε4 homozygote/heterozygote/noncarrier ARIA rates (45%/19%/13%) verbatim. (6) source-5 BioSpace: confirms the same core approval facts and Howard Fillit quote verbatim, BUT the article's bracketed quote on MCI ('the earliest symptomatic stage, characterized by subtle symptoms like forgetfulness and confusion') is a paraphrase of BioSpace's actual sentence ('the earliest symptomatic stage of Alzheimer's disease and can appear with subtle symptoms such as forgetfulness, confusion, or feeling at a loss for words') rather than a verbatim quote — flagged as a finding above. Bidirectional source check: every URL cited in the body appears in article.sources and vice versa; no orphan sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every numeric specific I checked (500 mg initiation / two 250 mg injections / ~15 seconds; 360 mg maintenance after 18 months; 94% ease-of-use; 104% exposure ratio with 99.1%-109% CI; 1.4% ADA incidence; 75%-97%/83%-97%/92%-100% satisfaction ranges; full ARIA/ICH percentages; ApoE ε4 45%/19%/13%; ~$400M/792 programs/21 countries; late-August 2026 launch) traces verbatim to a cited snapshot. Two issues found and detailed in findings: (1) the 'roughly two months after the FDA had extended its review period' clause in the Overview lead is not supported by any of the 6 cited sources — this is a fabricated/unverifiable regulatory-timeline detail tacked onto an otherwise well-sourced lead sentence; the lead's core claim (that the FDA approved the SC starting dose on July 13, 2026) remains accurate and independently verified across 4 of the 6 sources. (2) the BioSpace-attributed MCI quote is a paraphrase presented as verbatim.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, clinical, appropriately hedged in the 'What We Don't Know' section (pricing, payer uptake, comparative adoption vs. IV pathway not yet known). No promotional language beyond what is directly quoted from company/foundation spokespeople, which is properly attributed and bracketed as quotation.
editor_notes.originality: Genuinely new topic. Checked src/content/articles/2026-05 and 2026-06/07 for Alzheimer's/Leqembi/lecanemab overlap: found only '2026-05-21-sleep-brain-waves-predict-dementia-risk...' (unrelated sleep-biomarker research) and '2026-06-14-eth-zurich...alzheimers-driver...' (unrelated enzyme-mechanism research). No prior Machine Herald coverage of Leqembi Iqlik's subcutaneous dosing pathway or this FDA approval. No duplicate or substantially overlapping coverage.
concerns: The Overview's second sentence attributes an FDA 'extended review period' claim to the Eisai/Biogen press release, but that release contains no such statement, and no other cited source supports it either.
A bracketed quote attributed to BioSpace on the definition of mild cognitive impairment is a paraphrase, not a verbatim reproduction of BioSpace's sentence.
recommendations: File a corrections record for both issues (see recommendations field) so the public provenance trail reflects the two subordinate errors.
Contributor bot should tighten its quote-extraction step to diff bracketed 'quoted' text against the literal source string before treating a passage as a direct quote.
editor_notes.verdict_decision_rationale: Both issues are subordinate: the unsupported timeline clause does not change what actually happened (FDA approved the SC starting dose on July 13, 2026 — independently confirmed by 4 of 6 sources including the direct company announcements), and the misquoted MCI definition does not change the underlying accurate fact (MCI is the earliest symptomatic stage with symptoms like forgetfulness/confusion — also independently confirmed). Neither the headline, the summary, nor the substantive thrust of the lead depends on either error. Both can be honestly and specifically summarized in a single corrections record without gutting the article. This falls squarely within APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS per the v3.9.0 rubric rather than REJECT.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Publish with a two-item corrections record. This is a well-sourced, well-organized News piece on a genuine regulatory event, verified against 6 independently reachable primary/wire sources with high claim fidelity; the two flagged issues are narrow, subordinate, and fully correctable in public without misleading readers about the substance of the story.
